title: Skin and gut bacterial assemblages show differential responses to prolonged heat exposure and cooling in zebrafish (Danio rerio)
content:
Abstract

Rising water temperatures can disrupt host-associated microbial communities important to fish metabolism, immunity and pathogen defence; however, the effects of prolonged thermal exposure and subsequent recovery remain poorly understood. We examined skin and gut bacterial assemblages of juvenile zebrafish under four temperature regimes: T1 (28°C for 60 days), T2 (28°C for 30 days followed by 34°C for 30 days), T3 (34°C for 30 days followed by 28°C for 30 days) and T4 (34°C for 60 days). Bacterial assemblages were profiled on days 1, 30 and 60 using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing and analysis of resulting bacterial amplicon sequence variants. Gut community composition was comparatively stable across thermal treatments and showed limited overlap with water assemblages. In contrast, skin communities showed marked thermal sensitivity, with shifts in beta diversity, species richness and the relative abundance of commensal and potentially opportunistic taxa. Chronic heat exposure enriched Lysobacter, Rubrivivax, Gemmobacter and Pseudomonas and reduced Rhodobacter. Following cooling, T3 skin communities shifted towards control profiles, with increased overlap in core taxa, but did not fully return to the control state. These findings demonstrate tissue-specific responses to prolonged warming and identify the skin bacterial community as a potential non-invasive indicator of thermal perturbation and recovery.
